HOW MANY ARRIVE PER PICK - the single strongest lever on what the water is made of, which is why all 19 of these are here rather than in config.js. The spawner spends its per-tick budget in CREATURES: a school pick buys a whole school and a shark pick buys one shark, so a roster of 6-14 schools made the arena 75-81% minnows by headcount at every point in a run and the big-body share FELL from 22% at level 10 to 7% at level 21. Only fish.group.max used to live in this file; every other school's numbers were whatever the tuner last saved, so editing config.js did nothing. Measured by npm run test:ramp.

IT CIRCLES INSTEAD OF COMING AT ME. How much of the circling a body gives up while it is still OUTSIDE its stand-off ring. At 0 the radial and tangential terms are the same size however far out of position the body is, so it steers a flat 45 degrees off the player and closes at 71% of its own speed forever - measured, that was the four chasing bosses reading 45-49 degrees off the seal on every frame they were not mid-run, on every kind of player. At 1 the circling fades to nothing a full ring out and is at full strength only once the body has arrived, so the ring is still a ring and the way IN is a line. SHARED OUT AMONG WHOEVER IS COMPETING FOR THE RING, in code rather than here: a body alone takes the whole number and a pack divides it, because the same circling that is dead time for one boss is what fans six sharks out instead of stacking them on one line. Applies only on the way in - inside the ring the orbit is untouched, which is what a boss carrying the seal in its jaws is doing.

HOW CLOSE TO THE HEAD A BITE HAS TO LAND TO COST ANYTHING, as a fraction of the biting creature's own radius, before the seal's hit radius is added. The narrower of the bite's two gates: playerReach above (times `lead`) decides when the mouth starts OPENING, about twenty-five units out on a boss; this decides whether the teeth reached you. 0.55 of a radius is the front of the animal and nothing else - on the megalodon that is 5.0 units around a container origin sitting 3.9 in front of the snout and 21.9 in front of the fluke, so it covers the head with a little room and stops well short of the body. Widening it until the two gates agree would put a megalodon's bite damage on its tail. It has a row because it did not: the number was in imported-tuning.json and in no table, so a saved snapshot was its only real home and an edit to config.js could never have moved it - the same failure as the laser and the deck guns. tools/boss-bite-test.mjs holds it against the real bodies and npm run test:attack watches the panel that drags it.

HOW HARD THE WATER IS. 1 is the tuned game; 0.5 is half, 2 is twice. Multiplied into hp, damage, speed and aggression where each is baked onto a creature at spawn, so it rides on TOP of both run ramps and a creature already on screen keeps what it was born with.

of the dial above, how much goes into HEALTH - as an exponent, so 1 is the full dial and 0 leaves the stat alone. The four axes are deliberately unequal; see the note on CONFIG.pace.axes. Moving this does nothing while pace.enemy sits at 1, which is the right way round.

Boss weak spots. Glowing sores on the outer edge of a boss's silhouette that crit when shot and burst when they've swallowed enough - systems/bossHotSpots.js.

Fewest a boss can roll on arrival. The floor is 1 and the code clamps to it as well: a boss with no weak spot is missing a mechanic the player has been taught to look for on every other one, and in the water that is indistinguishable from the feature being broken.
Most a boss can roll. Read against the pool (CONFIG.hotSpots.pool, 12) - a boss's spots plus the ones still fading off the last corpse have to fit.

What a hit inside a spot is worth. Only the sources that AIM get it - bullets, the club swing, the strike. Auras and rings deliberately never crit; they cannot aim, so they would just be multiplying their own tick rate.

Damage (after critMul) that bursts one, as a fraction of the boss's max hp. THE NUMBER THAT DECIDES HOW LONG A SPOT STAYS PUT. At 0.06 a spot was gone in a couple of seconds of focused fire and the fight was mostly the gap between them - the colour shift, the doubling throb and the growing leak never had time to read. At 0.14 a boss with three spots carries nearly half its bar in weak points.
Wait before a burst spot is replaced elsewhere on the perimeter. This gap IS the cost of popping one - for these seconds the fight is an ordinary fight.

Spot size as a fraction of the WHOLE boss's radius. This is the crit's reach AND the drawn boundary - one number, read from one place, on purpose, which means making a spot more obvious costs reach and there is no way around that. Not a fraction of the hitbox sphere it sits on: a megalodon's biggest fitted sphere is 1.9 units against a body whose reach is 5, so that reading pinned every spot at minRadius and this number did nothing.
Cap on that size, as a multiple of the hitbox sphere the spot landed on. Stops a spot on a fin tip being drawn several times the size of the fin with a crit reach out over open water.
Floor on that size. Below about this a spot is a light nobody can reliably hit.
Ceiling on it. Above about this a spot stops being a place to aim at and becomes a region.

How far apart two spots try to sit, in multiples of the boss's own radius. A preference, not a rule - on a small body there may be no candidate far enough away, and a hard floor there would mean the second and third silently never appear.

Size of the burst when one goes, on top of the spot's own size. The emitter's size and speed move together behind this - that is the only lever that makes a fusing mass bigger without changing what it is made of.
Angular samples per hitbox sphere when hunting the outline. Runs once per arrival and once per rupture, never per frame.
The spot size the rupture burst was authored against, in world units. Only exists so ruptureScale above means '1 is as authored' - a bigger spot throws a proportionally bigger mass.

How far out along the skin the per-hit bleed is born, in multiples of the spot's radius. Not zero: fired from the centre the lobes fuse into a disc that sits ON the light and hides both the hot core and the hit flash.

How wide a tube around a candidate's own ray counts as the same piece of body when the point is resolved onto the mesh, as a fraction of the hitbox sphere it came from. Candidates sit on the rim of a FITTED sphere and a sphere is not the animal - on the megalodon that rim runs up to 1.18 units outside the mesh, and with the glow painted on the skin a centre off the body loses the whole bright middle of the patch.

How far inboard of the outline a spot's centre is pulled, in fractions of its own radius. Not zero: the glow is painted on the skin, so a centre exactly on the silhouette wastes half its circle over open water and the boundary ring - the thing that makes it read as a target - is off the body for most of its length. Keep under 1 or the spot stops touching the outline at all.

The kraken. How fast it swims while laying its ink ring - and since the weave is the fight's default state, this IS the squid's swimming speed. It was 13 against a roster row of 3.5 that calls this the slowest body in the game; measured, 99.9% of a fight ran at exactly 13.00. A little under twice its cruise reads as a move with intent rather than a sprint, and costs the trap nothing (5 crushes per 60s here against 6 at 13) - what closes the ring is the cloud's lifetime, not how fast the animal gets round.
The kraken. Seconds of weaving before it abandons a ring it cannot close and regroups. The cloud has a lifetime, so a ring open this long is one whose earliest wall is already dissolving.

The kraken. Seconds of ordinary circling after a failed trap, at the creature's own cruise. This is the fight's rhythm and it did nothing at all until the WEAVE branch grew a condition to match - the squid dropped straight back into weaving on the next frame. Zero here means the boss never rests.

The kraken. How fast the lunge travels once committed. This one is ALLOWED to be quick - it is a 0.8s dash down a heading it cannot correct, paid for by a ring that took seconds to build and a 0.9s wind-up. Read against weaveSpeed above: the gap between them is the difference between the animal moving and the animal attacking.

The kraken. How fast it creeps toward the player during the lunge's wind-up. Not zero: facing is read off the direction of travel, so a boss holding perfectly still keeps whatever heading it had and the tell stops saying WHERE.

The kraken. What the lunge multiplies its contact damage by for the 0.8s of the dash, billed as an ATTACK rather than as chip (see `ramming`) so it draws on the fight's whole per-second budget instead of the quarter-bar overlap ceiling. It was 3.2, and read against the rest of the roster that is the single biggest hit any boss lands: the megalodon's lunge perk is 2x and its bite is a fixed 24. This is still comfortably the biggest, and it still has to be - the player had two separate chances not to be here, a ring that took seconds to close and a 0.9s wind-up - but at 3.2 landing one was most of a bar and the fight was decided by whether a single dash connected.

THE SQUID ATTACKS TOO RARELY. The kraken. Seconds after a lunge recovers before the ring may commit another one. Cut from 7 with the chasing bosses' own cooldowns and for the same measured reason: a settle stacked on a cooldown was most of every boss fight. This one also sits behind trap.giveUp and trap.regroup, so the ring has to close before it is even asked - 3.6 is the gap AFTER all of that, not instead of it.

THE CRAB ATTACKS TOO RARELY. The king crab's gun. Seconds between volleys. Cut from 4.5: it sits UNDER `settle` below, which is the one that actually runs after a completed volley, so the pair was 9.5s of quiet for a 1.7s attack. Both halves had to move or cutting either one did nothing.

THE CRAB ATTACKS TOO RARELY. ...and the longer gap after a volley that actually FINISHED, as opposed to one the player interrupted. Cut from 5. Still the longer of the pair, which is the shape it always had: finishing the volley is the crab getting what it wanted and it pays for that.

THE CRAB ATTACKS TOO RARELY. The big overhead swing. Seconds before it may swing again. Cut from 7. It is gated on reach as well (haymakerRange, 2.6 x the claw's own), so this is the gap between swings the player is standing close enough to eat - not a gap in the fight.
THE CRAB ATTACKS TOO RARELY. ...and the gap after one that connected. Cut from 4.5, with the cooldown above.

THE CRAB ATTACKS TOO RARELY. The pounce. Seconds before it may leave the ground again. Cut from 9. Gated on the run's level as well (jump.minLevel 10), so this only ever shortens a fight that already had the move.
THE CRAB ATTACKS TOO RARELY. ...and the gap after a landing. Cut from 6, with the cooldown above.

THE CRAB ATTACKS TOO RARELY. The grab. Seconds before it may take hold of you again. Cut from 11, and deliberately the longest of the crab's four - a grab is a hold, and systems/control.js spends a page on why a hold is the movement not happening.

How hard placement favours the big parts of the animal, as an exponent on the host hitbox sphere's radius. Linear (1) was enough while spots were small: a spot wider than the body part it sits on has its boundary ring hanging over open water where nothing paints it, and renders as a flat glowing snout rather than a marked zone with an edge. Cubed, the torso wins decisively over the tail fluke.
How loud a crit is on a FRESH spot, as a multiplier on the hotSpotHit event's scale - which reaches the leak's particle count, the shake, the glow, the ripple and the sound gain through one field.
...and on one about to burst. The gap between this and rampMin is the audible run-up to a rupture, for a player who is looking somewhere else.

How far the collision hull and the skin may disagree at a candidate, as a fraction of the spot's radius, before that place is refused. The glow is painted on the flesh and every shot is resolved against the inflated hull, so where the two are far apart a bullet aimed at the light registers its hit somewhere else - measured, a dead-centre shot paid out on 25% of tries at the squid and 42% at the yacht against 100% at the orca. This is what makes the glowing area and the collision shape the same area.

Whether working a weak spot kicks BIG CHUM loose at all. This meat is FUEL - swallowing a piece refills boost pips, not health - which is deliberately a different currency from the health chunk a boss throws on a timer (chumChunk.boss in spawning.csv). That one is a break the fight hands you; this is the fight paying for aim.

Crit damage into ONE spot between pieces, as a fraction of the pool that ruptures it (hotSpots.ruptureFraction). Not per hit: an automatic weapon lands ten times a second and the club once, so counting hits would make one a chum fountain and the other pay nothing. At 0.34 a spot sheds two pieces on the way to its burst whatever is chewing it.

What one piece is worth in BOOST PIPS. Read against the bar: five pips is a whole meter by default (pipCount derives it from strike.chumRefill), so 2 is a strike's worth of two pieces and one worked spot is most of a bar.

How many pieces the BURST throws, on top of whatever the damage on the way in already bought. The rupture is the moment a spot is worth the most and it should read that way in the water - a spray of meat, not one more lump.
...and what each of those is worth in boost pips. Bigger than hotSpots.chum.pips on purpose: popping one is the thing the whole run-up was for.

How hard a piece is thrown clear of the spot (u/s), out along the skin's normal - toward the player, because a spot is somewhere they aimed. Water drag is exponential (pickups.toss.waterDrag 4.5), so a piece travels about tossSpeed/4.5 units: at 13 it settled against the flank still inside the animal's silhouette, at 42 it clears the body in a straight line and lands in open water. The goo trail behind it is a statement about that speed - there is nothing to draw at a drift.

Radians either side of that normal. Narrow: a full circle is right for a chunk thrown off a body nobody is next to, and wrong for meat leaving a place the player is shooting at - and the straighter the line, the more the trail behind it reads as a shot rather than a spray.
Where a piece is born, out along the normal in multiples of the spot's radius. Same reason hotSpots.bleedOffset is not zero - born on the centre it sits on top of the light it came out of.

Seconds before an uncollected piece leaves the water. Far shorter than the ambient chunk's 34, and that gap is the difference between the two pickups: a chunk is worth crossing the arena for, this is fuel for the fight it fell out of.

Ceiling on pieces and health chunks in the water at once. A boss with three spots worked by a fast weapon can otherwise carpet the arena, and a pickup you cannot avoid stops being a reward for aiming.

Speed (u/s) below which a thrown piece stops being IN FLIGHT and becomes an ordinary pickup. One number, two jobs, because they are the same fact: above it the piece lays a goo trail and the food magnet may not claim it, below it the piece lies in the water like any other. The magnet half is what makes the throw visible - reach is 6 units before upgrades and the whole magnet radius during a chain, and the magnet outranks a throw and cancels it, so without this gate a piece kicked out near the seal is claimed on its first frame and appears to spawn at the mouth. Nothing is lost by waiting: drag brings any throw under this within half a second.

Whether bursting a weak spot shoves the boss. A rupture is a charge going off inside a body, and without this everything about it - the goo, the shake, the meat, the sound - happens around an animal that carries on swimming its line as though nothing had gone off in its flank.

How hard, as a multiple of what a FULL-CHARGE ram delivers (strike.knockback, applied through the same applyKnockback so it lands on one integrator, resists on the boss's own size curve and brings the skeleton flinch with it). Thrown out along the skin's normal AT THE SPOT, so a wound opened on the near flank pushes the animal away from the player and one on the far side pulls it across. Over 1 on purpose: a ram is the seal leaning on the animal with its whole body, this is an explosion under its skin.

IT WANDERS INSTEAD OF ATTACKING. bossShark lunge: seconds after a run recovers before it may commit another. Cut from 4.0, which was itself cut from 8.5 for the same complaint one step further back - a boss that chips you between attacks rather than attacking you. Measured over 90-second fights against a parked, a strolling and a sprinting seal, `rest` was 52-60% of every fight on every chasing boss: the single biggest block of the fight was the cooldown. gap (units) inside which a barracuda may commit to a run. THE SHORT, CONSTANT VERSION OF THE PASS - a barracuda arrives in a shiver and jabs from close range rather than crossing the arena, so read every number on these eight rows against the sharks' above and expect them to be about half. These eight and the sailfish's below arrived here for the reason every other block in this file did: they were in imported-tuning.json and in no table, so a saved snapshot beat config.js and an edit there could never have moved them.
closer than this and there is no wind-up left worth watching, so it does not start one.
seconds of the tell. Short, because a barracuda is quick and the threat is the shiver rather than the individual.
how much of its cruise speed it keeps while gathering. Not zero - the turn onto you is the tell, and a body that hovers holds whatever heading it arrived on.
dash speed as a multiple of its cruise. Barely more than double a shark's cruise multiplier in absolute terms; this is a jab, not a charge.
seconds of committed run. Read against range x speedMul: the run has to carry past where you were or the dodge is unreadable.
radians/sec it may lean onto you DURING the run. The commitment is the whole effect - raise this far and the jab becomes a homing shot.
seconds after a pass before it may open another. The shortest in the roster on purpose - a shiver jabbing constantly is what a barracuda swarm is.

gap (units) inside which a sailfish may commit. IT IS NOT AN OVERLAY ON A HUNT - the sailfish has behavior: chase and the lunge IS its whole behaviour, so these eight decide everything it does rather than the last stretch of an approach. Same snapshot-only history as the barracuda's above.
closer than this it BACKS OFF, unlike the hunters, which do not need to - `hunt` keeps a standoff of its own and this behaviour has none.
seconds of the tell - throttled, turning onto you, the ring drawing in.
how much of its cruise it keeps while gathering.
dash speed as a multiple of its cruise. The fastest animal in the ocean, and the number that says so.
seconds of committed run.
radians/sec it may lean onto you during the run.
seconds between passes. Long, because one sailfish is a solitary animal making a deliberate pass rather than a pack jabbing.

radians off horizontal the line to the seal may sit at for a run to be opened. The SHARED lungeRules.maxPitch is 1.0 (57 deg) and exists for wildlife: a shark that could lunge straight up at a seal hovering over it would not have to earn your depth by making passes, which is where a shark's threat comes from. A swimming boss carries lateral.flip false and its own cruisePitch and turns through three dimensions already, so holding its COMMIT to a flat cone is the one place left that still says tank. At 1.45 (83 deg) it can open a run from almost anywhere it can swim, which is the whole point of letting it swim there. Measured: the pitch gate held these four up for 20-40% of a fight at 1.0.

double/feint: seconds of the throttled second gather between two runs

The CEILING on a re-aim, in seconds. The step's own reaimTime is the FLOOR: what a body needs between two runs of a double or a feint is however long it takes to come round onto the seal, which is a turn of up to 180 degrees over a turn rate spanning 3.4 rad/s (a hammerhead) down to 1.05 (a boss shark). A flat number could not work and did not - at 0.45s a boss shark turned 27 degrees of the 180 it wanted and committed anyway, a median 107 degrees off the player and past 90 two times in three, on 60% of that archetype's lunges. This is the other end: a re-aim that ran as long as the turn wanted would be a boss floating gently for three seconds in the middle of its own attack, which reads as the animal having lost interest. At 1.3 the slowest turners sit right on it (npm run test:lungeaim prints the medians), and the mosasaur abandons about one plan in six rather than dawdling.

how much of the constant-velocity INTERCEPT a wind-up aims at. 0 aims at where you are - which is what every lunge in the game did until now, and the whole of why a committed run misses a player who is doing anything at all. Measured with npm run aim: the wind-up converges to a median ZERO degrees off on every archetype, so the body is perfectly aimed at the moment it commits, at a point the seal has already left by the time 22 units a second of run gets there - and strikeTurnRate x strikeTime is ten to seventeen degrees of correction across the whole roster, which cannot cover it. There was never anything wrong with the aim; there was no aim. A FRACTION because both ends are wrong: at 0 a shark lands 3.3u from a seal it must be within 1.66 of and connects 0% against a dodging player, and at 1 it connects 100% and the dodge is gone. At 0.55 the same dodging player is missed by 2.0u instead of 3.3u and a normally-moving one is hit 92% of the time against 87%. SHIPS AT 0, deliberately: tools/shark-lunge-test.mjs asserts that a seal swimming across a shark nose is MISSED on six archetypes, which is this game statement about what a pass IS, and any lead at all starts breaking it. The mechanism is measured and ready and turning it on is a design decision, not a bug fix. Move this first if lunges feel harmless or feel unfair. Per-species override on the def own lunge.lead.

How close to pointed at you, in radians, a body has to be at the END of a re-aim for the second run to happen at all. Wider than this and the plan is ABANDONED - cooldown, veer off, exactly as a finished pass does. THIS IS THE GUARANTEE and it is worth more than the retimed re-aim beside it: reaimMax is a real ceiling, and a body that has been shoved, chilled or simply out-turned can reach the end of one still facing the wrong way. A committed run is the most expensive thing one of these does - unshovable, armoured (CONFIG.boss.armor) and on a boss carrying four times its contact damage - and a player who dodged one has earned the miss. What they have not earned is watching three tonnes of animal charge empty water on the far side of the arena. 1.05 is about 60 degrees, wide on purpose: a run that misses BY A BODY is the fight working, and only a run that was never pointed at you is the bug.
double: the second run is strikeTime x this
feint: seconds of the fake first run
feint: the fake run is the real burst speed x this

IT FLINCHES INSTEAD OF ATTACKING. The master switch for the whole rule: 0 and a boss answers to being shot at exactly like wildlife does, which is the game before this existed - a stream of pellets buckles it every few frames and the answer to a wind-up is to shoot harder instead of to move.

...how much of the ORDINARY per-hit flinch a boss still takes (1 = all of it, like a shark). This is the twitch and the skeleton shove from a pellet landing anywhere on the body. At 0 a boss under fire does not buckle at all; raise it if bosses read as bulletproof rather than as heavy.

...and how much of the ordinary KNOCKBACK it takes from anything not on the sources list below - every projectile, a headstone, a release burst, a pickup blast. At 0 only the named three move a boss at all.

IT GETS INTERRUPTED MID-ATTACK. 1 refuses every flinch and every shove while a boss is attacking - the wind-up, the run, the grab, the crab's pinch and a perk-driven move (see isAttacking in entities/enemies.js). Turn it off to feel the bug: the animal is whipped through its own tell and the attack reads as cancelled. The ONE thing still allowed to break an attack is a perfect strike into a lit weak spot; that lives in weapons.csv under strike.weakSpot.stagger.

IT NEVER ZAPS ME. How far from the ESCA (not the body) the anglerfish will decide to fire at all. Was 34 against an arena 184.9 wide, so from most of the water it did nothing; measured over 60-second fights from eight stations it fired zero beams from seven of them. 190 is the corner-to-corner diagonal. Keep it at or under beamLength below or it charges shots that stop short.
...and how far the beam actually carries. The pair with lureRange above: the reach of the decision and the reach of the shot have to agree.

IT ATTACKS TOO RARELY. Seconds before the next LURE attack, armed by any attack including the lunge. Was 5.6, which made it the pacemaker and left dead lurk on top of the stages; at 0.6 the cadence is the cycle instead (charge 1.25 + discharge 0.55 + lureRecover 0.45 + settle 0.6, about a shot every 2.9s). Keep it above 0 so a lunge and a beam cannot land on the same breath.

...the gap after a beam or radial specifically, separate from recoverTime which the melee LUNGE pays. A spent beam is a light going out; a spent lunge is a whole body stranded across the water. Sharing one number was most of the reason this boss read as idle.
...and the lunge's own recovery - the window a player who dodged the melee pass gets for free. Deliberately the longer of the two.

IT ZAPS ME WITH NO WARNING. Seconds of the lit-lure tell before a beam or radial fires. MUST EQUAL emissiveCues.charge.attack or the light stops peaking on the frame the thing fires - tools/boss-angler-test.mjs asserts it.

IT FIRES OUT OF ITS OWN BACK. Rad/s the body turns to face you while it is waiting. The lure hangs off the front of the head, so a fish that has not come round shoots through its own body. Was 0.9 - slow enough to swim behind it, which was real counterplay when its reach was 34 and buys nothing now that it shoots across the arena.

...and rad/s while it is CHARGING, which is the snap onto the line. Still a rate rather than a lock, so a seal that keeps moving across the charge makes it commit off - the only counterplay the beam has, and the only one it needs.
...inside this it bites instead of shooting. Three ranges, three answers: bite here, hold inside pulseRadius, zap beyond it.

IT HOLDS ME WHEN IT SHOULD ZAP ME (or the reverse). The radial's reach, and the circle its tell is drawn at - the two are one number or the tell is a lie. Anything past this times pulsePick gets the beam instead.

IT NEVER COMES NEAR ME. The chance each wander roll is taken toward the seal instead of anywhere at all. At 0 (the old behaviour, and still what every jellyfish and the turtle do) the drift is a random walk: measured, this boss sat a mean 80 units from a parked seal and spent 93% of a 90-second fight more than 40 units away. At 0.75 it is 44 and 47%. It is a drift with a DIRECTION, not a chase - the body still moves at 1.6 u/s and cannot catch anybody, which is what its damage zones are priced on.

...how loosely it aims when it does lean. Wide (1.1 rad either side) so it still reads as drifting rather than homing. Narrowing this is nearly free - at lean 1 and cone 0.5 the mean only improves 44 to 41 - so the real remaining lever is enemies.csv's speed column for this body, not this.
...and how often it picks a new direction at all.
rad off horizontal a lateral hunter may swim at when not lunging (~24 deg) - the one number that says sharks swim left and right
rad off horizontal on a deliberate act on fixed food - a fish or a scrap of chum - looser than the cruise, still not vertical
rad of wanted turn past which a lateral hunter comes about (mirrors its heading, yaws through the camera) instead of arcing through vertical
swim speed through the come-about, x cruise - it slows to turn rather than skidding round nose-backwards
seconds after one come-about before a lateral hunter may do another - a body sitting on what it wants sees the wanted direction reverse every frame, and without a hold it vibrated in place

seconds between a deck gun deciding to fire and the throw - and, since the tell was added, the whole of the warning the player gets. It was 0.45 with nothing at all on screen for any of it, which is a delay rather than a wind-up. Read against the seal's swim speed: this has to be long enough to clear the line a fish is already aimed down. The blink that runs through it is a slider (boats.guns.fx.tell).

world units from hull to seal beyond which no deck gun fires. A boat crossing the far side of the arena stays a target rather than a turret. Read against the arena's 80-unit width - much past half of that and there is nowhere in the water a boat cannot reach.

how much of the compounding enemy damage ramp (spawn.ramp.damage) a deck gun rides, 0 = none, 1 = exactly what a creature's contact damage pays. Taken of the ramp's EXCESS over 1, so difficulty 0 is always the tier row's own number. A creature has to be TOUCHED and the whole game is about not touching things; a gun reaches thirty units at a seal doing nothing wrong, and on the full ramp one fish passed the seal's entire starting bar at the ten-minute mark.

ceiling on what any ONE deck-gun shot may be worth, as a fraction of player.maxHp - the base bar, not the player's current one, so a health card never makes the boats hit harder. The backstop on the far end of the ramp share above. Deliberately well under player.damageCap.perSecond (0.9): that one is a ceiling on everything inside a second, and a boat reaching it alone would mean the cap had quietly become the boats' tuning.

what one small fry off a deck is worth at difficulty 0. INDEX 0 IS THE `fish` TIER - the rows here are positional because tiers is an array, and npm run test:boatguns asserts each index still holds the id this note names. Was 6.
shortest reload for the fish tier, seconds. The per-boat pick is random between this and cooldownMax so two hulls never fire in lockstep. Was 2.8.
longest reload for the fish tier, seconds. Was 4.6.

what one trout is worth at difficulty 0. INDEX 1 IS THE `trout` TIER. Read against tiers.1.count, which is 2: this row is worth double what it says per volley, which is why it took the deepest cut of the three. Was 10.
trout per volley. The tier's identity - you cannot sidestep a pair arriving spread out the way you sidestep one fish.
shortest reload for the trout tier, seconds. Was 2.6.
longest reload for the trout tier, seconds. Was 4.2.
what one sailfish is worth at difficulty 0. INDEX 2 IS THE `sailfish` TIER - the heaviest thing a hull throws, one per volley, and the fastest. Was 16.
shortest reload for the sailfish tier, seconds. Was 3.
longest reload for the sailfish tier, seconds. Was 4.6.

reload multiplier for a trawler's deck gun - below 1 is faster, so 0.8 is a quarter more shots than a plain boat. The trawler is the bigger, tougher hull and this is the rest of what makes it the worse one to leave afloat.

seconds an artillery trawler's anti-air takes to come up. Longer than the fish gun's on purpose: it fires at a seal in the air, which is the one place the seal has least control over where it is going. Was 0.6.
seconds between anti-air volleys. Volleys alternate mussel, gull, mussel, gull, so this is the gap between EITHER kind. Was 3.6.
what one homing mussel is worth at difficulty 0, before its blast. Two per volley. Was 14.
what the bad gull is worth at difficulty 0. One per volley, the heaviest single thing a hull throws, and it chases. Was 18.

multiples of a gun's own firing range that the shot it fires must be able to cross, at its own speed. The flight is DERIVED from this rather than typed per gun - see CONFIG.enemyShot. 2 is "it can just reach a stationary seal at maximum range and stop dead"; the excess over 2 is what pays for the seal swimming away from it and, on a seeker, for the curve being longer than the line. The row's own `life` still wins where it is the longer of the two, so nothing already generous is shortened. The bug this fixes: the boat's fish tier flew 11 u/s for 3s - 33 units against a gun that opens up at 30 - so a shot fired at anything past point blank closed on a 9 u/s seal at two units a second and ran out of fuse before it arrived.
whether hostile shots can be shot out of the air at all. 0 puts every gun in the game back to the way it was: you dodge it or you wear it.

how much player fire it takes to clear one hostile shot at difficulty 0, before the per-difficulty ramp and the share of its own damage below. Read against a starting build's damage per pellet - at 7 an opening shot takes one or two pellets, which is the right price for a counterplay that is supposed to be available rather than free.

added to a shot's toughness per point of run difficulty. A boss arrives every fifth level and difficulty is what tracks that, so this is what makes a late-run volley take real fire to clear rather than evaporating on contact with a built-out seal.

...plus this much per point of the shot's OWN damage. One number instead of a toughness column per gun: a sailfish off a deck hits three times as hard as a minnow and should not swat as easily, and taking the difference off the damage the shot already carries means every gun in the game is covered including any added later.

how much of a piercing pellet's pierce budget clearing one hostile shot costs. 1 means a hostile shot counts exactly like a body; 0 would let a single piercing pellet sweep a whole volley for nothing.
